name: Lachish
title: City in Judah besieged by the Assyrians
summary: Lachish was an important fortified city in the kingdom of Judah, strategically located in the southwest of the land. The city is best known for being besieged and conquered by the Assyrian king Sennacherib in 701 BC, as well as for having served as a refuge for King Amaziah. Although Lachish is primarily a place name and not a person, the city is mentioned in several important biblical contexts related to the kings and prophets of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Joshua's conquest of Lachish
keyEvents.description: During the conquest of Canaan, Joshua attacked Lachish and captured the city, striking down all its inhabitants with the sword.

keyEvents.title: Fortification under Rehoboam
keyEvents.description: King Rehoboam fortified Lachish as one of the defense cities in Judah to protect the kingdom's southwestern border.

keyEvents.title: King Amaziah's flight to Lachish
keyEvents.description: When a conspiracy was made against King Amaziah in Jerusalem, he fled to Lachish, but was pursued and killed there.

keyEvents.title: Sennacherib's Siege of Lachish
keyEvents.description: The Assyrian king Sennacherib besieged and captured Lachish during his campaign against Judah in 701 BC, and from there sent his envoys to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The Prophet Micah's Warning to Lachish
keyEvents.description: The prophet Micah warned Lachish and called the city a starting point of sin for the daughter of Zion, because the city had followed the sins of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Lachish under Nebuchadnezzar's Attack
keyEvents.description: During Nebuchadnezzar's campaign against Judah, Lachish was one of the last cities to hold out along with Azekah, as described by the prophet Jeremiah.
